name: Clothing chest of drawers (isho-dansu), two stacked parts (kasane-dansu)
era_note: Tansu appear in Osaka in the Kanbun era (1661-73) and spread from the Shotoku era (1711-16); still costly in 1730, so T2-3 only [N06, BUILD_LIST row 26]

references.kind: surviving farmhouse (Former Kasuya house, Itabashi), period_image in build_list.json
references.shows: stacked chests of drawers, dark worn wood, iron corner fittings and a U carrying handle on the side, ring pulls

references.kind: museum reconstruction (Fukagawa Edo Museum, Tenpo era, c.1840)
references.shows: a two-part tansu: two drawers per part, two ring pulls per drawer, a round plate at the centre of each drawer, iron corner plates at the joint between the parts

caveat: Neither photo is a dated 1730 object: i01 shows chests kept in a surviving house, i07 is a c.1840 reconstruction. The form (two stacked boxes, iron ring pulls, corner irons, side handles) is common to both and to the build list.

parts_m.built: lower 0.00-0.50, upper 0.50-1.00; the upper part is 4 mm smaller at the front and sides so the two boxes read

drawers.built: upper: two small (0.466 x 0.166) over one wide lock drawer (0.948 x 0.266); lower: two wide (0.956 x 0.216)

board_m.reason: tansu carcass boards are about 2 cm; the front frame shows the board edges

ring_pull_m.reason: scaled from i07 against the drawer height

lock_plate_d_m.reason: round plate at the centre of the wide drawers, as in i07

side_handle_m.reason: U handle hanging flat against the side, as in i01

palette.body: timber_interior wanted (jp_m_wood_interior not built); stand-in jp_m_wood_street_dark_w2, dE76 9.0
